## Review 2026-07-27 — Fourier ring correlation (`imaging/frc.py` + `img_frc`)

Slice: `e2d7ee0c0` (*FRC leaves CLSM Draw and becomes a resolution measurement*),
the freshest large landing and one with no findings on record — the shared kernel
`chisurf/core/fluorescence/imaging/frc.py`, the plugin `core.py`/`api`, the view
model and the tool. The maths that is written down is right: the ½-bit and 2σ
formulae match van Heel & Schatz, the rings are binned on normalised frequency so
a strip resolves like a square, and the pixel-size scaling carries through. What
does not hold is what happens at the *edges* of that maths — the threshold
crossing is extrapolated rather than interpolated whenever the curve starts below
its own threshold (S1, wrong and even negative resolutions on real dim data), the
FFT is taken on the raw halves so every non-periodic image reads ~1.4–2.7× finer
than it is, and an odd-sized image silently loses a row and a column of Fourier
space. All three are invisible to the test suite because every test image is
even-sized and exactly periodic (built with `ifft2`) and every crossing test uses
the default criterion. Findings RF-408..RF-411.

### RF-408
- **Status:** FIXED
- **Severity:** S1 (the threshold crossing is extrapolated outside the two rings it claims to interpolate between — the reported resolution can be an order of magnitude off, or negative)
- **Location:** `chisurf/core/fluorescence/imaging/frc.py:300-322` (`resolve`: the `start` skip loop, the first-`below` search, then `previous = index - 1` and `weight = gap_before / (gap_before - gap_now)`)
- **Finding:** the interpolation assumes ring `previous` sits *above* its threshold, and nothing ever checks it. Two routes violate that. (a) `start` is advanced past every ring whose count-clipped threshold is `>= 1.0`, so `previous = start - 1` is a ring the search deliberately excluded. (b) Even with `start = 1`, ring 0 can be below its threshold. Either way `gap_before < 0`, the weight is no longer in `[0, 1]`, and the "crossing" lands anywhere. Verified on a dim but perfectly ordinary image — a field band-limited at 0.15 cycles/px (true limit 6.67 px), 128×128, ~0.3 counts/px, two independent Poisson draws: `half_bit` reports **52.6 px** (photon seed 2) and **84.0 px** (seed 4) where `fixed_1/7` reports 6.36–6.53 px on the same data; the returned crossing 0.01903 lies *outside* the bracket `[0.00391, 0.01172]` it was computed from, because `below[0..3]` are all True. Worse on data that resolves nothing: two independent white-noise 128×128 images under `two_sigma`, 30 seeds → **12 give a negative crossing frequency and a negative resolution** (down to −268.7 px) and 15 of 30 report a "resolution" finer than 10 px for halves that share nothing at all. The GUI prints the number verbatim (`gui/view_model.py:346`, `f"<h3>{result.resolution:.4g} {unit}</h3>"`), so a user sees `-40.86 px` as a headline. Take the first crossing *after* the curve has been above its threshold (require `values[previous] >= threshold[previous]`, else keep searching) and clamp the interpolated frequency into `[frequency[previous], frequency[index]]`. `test/fluorescence/test_frc.py:45` only exercises the default criterion, which is why this is green.
- **Fix note:** `resolve` now takes the first ring that is below its threshold **and whose predecessor is above it** (`if below[i] and not below[i - 1]`), i.e. the first genuinely *downward* crossing; a curve that never rises above its threshold returns `crossed=False` instead of an extrapolated number. That makes `gap_before >= 0 > gap_now` an invariant, so the weight is in `[0, 1]` and the crossing cannot leave `[frequency[previous], frequency[index]]` — no clamp needed, and the `gap_before == gap_now` special case (unreachable now, the denominator is strictly positive) is gone. Measured on the finding's own cases: two independent 128x128 noise fields, seed 0, went from **-4.90 px** (`half_bit`) and **-40.86 px** (`two_sigma`) to no crossing; a dim shot-noise image band-limited at 0.15 cycles/px reads 6.50 px under `two_sigma` where it read 44.89 px. Pinned by two new tests in `test/fluorescence/test_frc.py`: `test_the_crossing_is_interpolated_not_extrapolated` (dim Poisson pair, all three criteria must land within 30 % of the 6.67 px band limit) and `test_a_crossing_is_never_reported_outside_the_frequency_axis` (6 seeds x 3 criteria of unrelated noise: either no crossing, or a frequency inside the axis and a positive resolution) — both fail on the old code. `docs/concepts/frc_resolution.md` records that the count-dependent criteria now answer "no crossing" for halves that share nothing.

### RF-409
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (no apodization, so every non-periodic image — i.e. every real one — reports a resolution 1.4–2.7× finer than it is)
- **Location:** `chisurf/core/fluorescence/imaging/frc.py:173-176` (`f1 = np.fft.fft2(a)`, `f2 = np.fft.fft2(b)` on the raw halves), and the absence of any window in `chisurf/plugins/microscopy/img_frc/core.py:286-299` (`analyse`)
- **Finding:** the two halves are Fourier-transformed as they come. A real image does not wrap, so the discontinuity at its border leaks a cross-shaped pattern across the whole spectrum — and that pattern is *the same in both halves* (it is set by the object and the field of view, not by the noise), so it correlates perfectly and holds the FRC up in the band where the halves genuinely share nothing. Measured: band-limited object (cut-off 0.15 cycles/px, true limit 6.67 px), 256×256, shot noise, with a smooth left-to-right illumination ramp so the edges do not match — reported resolution **2.50 px** (crossing 0.400 cycles/px, i.e. nearly Nyquist); the same two halves multiplied by a Tukey(0.25) window give **5.90 px** (crossing 0.170). At 0.30 cycles/px, inside the pure-noise band, the unwindowed FRC still reads 0.256 against 1/7 = 0.143, while the windowed one reads −0.019; at 0.45 cycles/px, 0.143 vs −0.010. A plain non-periodic crop without any ramp shows the same in miniature: 4.67 px unwindowed vs 5.99 px windowed. Nieuwenhuizen et al. 2013 — the reference this module cites for the 1/7 criterion — apply a Tukey window for exactly this reason; neither `docs/concepts/frc_resolution.md` nor `chisurf/plugins/microscopy/img_frc/gui/help.md` mentions windowing at all. Apply a Tukey (or Hann) window to both halves before the FFT, ideally as a documented option that is on by default. The test suite cannot see this: `test/fluorescence/test_frc.py:16` builds its pairs with `ifft2`, so every test image is exactly periodic and leaks nothing.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-410
- **Status:** FIXED
- **Severity:** S2 (on an odd-sized image the highest positive frequency row and column are never accumulated, so the outer ring occupancies — which set the ½-bit and 2σ thresholds — are wrong)
- **Location:** `chisurf/core/fluorescence/imaging/frc.py:111-113` (`for xi in range(-(nx // 2), nx // 2)` / `for yi in range(-(ny // 2), ny // 2)` in `_ring_sums`)
- **Finding:** `range(-(n // 2), n // 2)` enumerates all `n` FFT frequencies only when `n` is even. For odd `n` it visits `n - 1` of them: it keeps `-n//2` and drops `+n//2`, the highest positive frequency, so the loop is not even conjugate-symmetric. Verified by summing the visited pixels: **4096 of 4225** for a 65×65 image (129 = 2·65−1 missing) and **15876 of 16129** for 127×127; nothing is dropped at 64×64 or 128×128. The loss is concentrated in the outermost rings, which is where the crossing lives: against a full-coverage reference the ring counts are off by 34 of 200 (17 %) in the last ring at 65×65 and by 46 of 388 at 129×129, and `counts` is exactly the input of `threshold_curve` for `half_bit` and `two_sigma`; the correlation values themselves differ by up to 0.046 (65×65) and 0.025 (129×129). Odd sizes are not exotic — a cropped ROI or an odd CLSM line count lands there — and no test in `test/fluorescence/test_frc.py` uses one. Iterate `range(-(nx // 2), (nx + 1) // 2)` on both axes (or bin from `np.fft.fftfreq`, which is what a reference implementation does).
- **Fix note:** both loops in `_ring_sums` now run `range(-(n // 2), (n + 1) // 2)`, the `n` indices `numpy.fft.fftfreq` enumerates — identical to the old bound for even `n`, one frequency longer for odd `n`. Measured coverage went from 4096 to 4225 of 4225 pixels at 65×65, 4032 → 4191 at 127×33 and 2048 → 2080 at 32×65; 64×64 is unchanged. The docstring records why the bound is `(n + 1) // 2`. Pinned by `test_every_fourier_pixel_lands_in_a_ring` in `test/fluorescence/test_frc.py`, parametrised over (65, 65), (64, 64), (127, 33) and (32, 65): the ring occupancies must sum to `nx * ny` *and* match, ring for ring, a reference built by binning the frequency grid directly with `numpy.bincount`, with the public `frc_curve` counts checked against the same reference over the rings it keeps. It fails on the old bound for all three odd shapes.

### RF-411
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S3 (the view model composes a specific failure message and the tool throws it away for a constant one)
- **Location:** `chisurf/plugins/microscopy/img_frc/gui/tool.py:91-95` (`_on_finished`: `self.model.status if ok else "Measurement failed"`) against `chisurf/plugins/microscopy/img_frc/gui/view_model.py:237-241` (`self._status = f"FRC failed: {exc}"`, and `:218-220` `"No image loaded."`)
- **Finding:** every way a measurement can fail carries a message that names the cause and the way out — `core.halves` raises "a frame split needs at least two frames; this source has 1 — use a channel split or a second file" (`core.py:210-214`), "the two channels of a channel split must differ", "split='two_files' needs a second file", `frc_curve` raises "the two halves differ in shape: … vs …" — `compute()` catches each of them into `self._status`, and `_on_finished` then discards it in favour of the constant "Measurement failed". The traceback goes to `logger.debug`, so nothing reaches the user at all: they see a two-word failure and no hint that the fix is a different split. Show `self.model.status` on the failure branch as well (it is always set before `compute` returns `False`). The sibling tools `img_drift` and `img_coloc` share the pattern, so fix them together.
- **Fix note:**

## Review 2026-07-27 — burst consumers: `tcspc.from_bursts` and `pch.from_bursts`

Slice: `508904848` (*advertise what consumes bursts, and add TCSPC + PCH
consumers*) — the freshest large landing, 500 new lines in
`chisurf/server/services/bursts.py` with no findings on record. The discovery
seam is sound: `bursts.consumers` merges the core JSON with plugin manifests,
plugin keys supersede core ones, and the companion repo's
`test_every_advertised_rpc_exists_on_the_server` really does resolve every
advertised name (core through `server_methods.json`, `burst_fcs.*` through the
plugin manifest). The `KNOWN_ROUTINES` guard against the tttrlib segfault is
right, and the interior-mode selection bias is documented in the module, the
result and the guide.

What does not hold is everything the 18 tests do not reach, and they all share
one blind spot: **every test drives a single file with two disjoint intervals.**
`burst_slices` is a `{path: intervals}` *mapping* precisely because a gate spans
files — and a two-file gate fails outright (RF-412). The other five are the
edges of the accounting: span-mode `n_photons` counts the span rather than the
gate (RF-413), `burst_duty_cycle` exceeds its documented `(0, 1]` on the very
overlapping intervals `_selected_indices` is tested to deduplicate (RF-414),
interior mode counts half-observed burst-edge bins as whole (RF-415), and a
channel number the file's routing dtype cannot hold becomes a server-side
`OverflowError` (RF-416). Findings RF-412..RF-417.

### RF-412
- **Status:** FIXED
- **Severity:** S1 (a gate spanning more than one file always fails, and a single-file decay gets a truncated, data-dependent time axis)
- **Location:** `chisurf/server/services/bursts.py:212-213` (`n_bins = int(micro.max()) + 1 if micro.size else 1`; `n_out = max(1, n_bins // max(1, int(coarsening)))`) and `:223` (`accum[i] = counts if accum[i] is None else accum[i] + counts`)
- **Finding:** the number of micro-time bins is taken from the **largest micro-time value observed in the file** instead of the header's `number_of_micro_time_channels`, so the decay length is data-dependent and two files essentially never agree. Since `accum[i] + counts` adds the per-file histograms elementwise, a multi-file gate — the only reason `burst_slices` is a mapping at all — raises `ValueError` and the whole request comes back as `OPERATION_FAILED`. Verified: two 2000-photon streams give `decay read failed: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (4095,) (2999,)`, and even two streams that both contain a photon at the top channel differ by one (`(4095,) (4096,)`). On the real test file `test/data/clsm/PQ_Olympus_MFIS.ht3` the observed maximum is **31277** while the header declares **32768** channels, so a single-file decay is 1491 bins short of the instrument axis and will not line up with an IRF or a background decay measured on the same setup. `coarsening` compounds it: `n_bins // coarsening` floors while `np.bincount` grows to `max(binned)+1`, so `coarsening=3` returns 1365 bins where the axis has 1366 (and `coarsening=8` happens to hide a one-tick difference between two files, so the failure is intermittent across gates). Take `n_bins` from `tttr.header.number_of_micro_time_channels` and size the output with `ceil(n_bins / coarsening)`. No test in `test/server/test_burst_services.py` passes more than one path.
- **Fix note:** new `_micro_time_bins(tttr, micro)` takes the axis from the header's `number_of_micro_time_channels` (floored at the occupied maximum, so a header that under-declares still cannot drop a photon), and `n_out` is now `ceil(n_bins / coarsening)` instead of a floor. Files whose TAC ranges genuinely differ are refused with a message naming both files and both ranges (`INVALID_INPUT`) rather than surfacing a NumPy broadcast error as `OPERATION_FAILED`. Pinned by four tests in `test/server/test_burst_services.py`: the real file's decay is the declared 32768 bins (not the occupied 31278); a two-file gate over synthetic streams with different occupied maxima sums; every `coarsening` in `1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 512` keeps both files on one axis of length `ceil(4096 / c)`; and two different TAC ranges give a clear error. The guide paragraph on the axis could not land in the same change — `docs/guides/52_send_bursts_to_analysis.md` is staged for deletion by a concurrent instance — so the contract is stated in the `from_bursts_decay` docstring instead.

### RF-413
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (`n_photons` reports the photons in the span, not in the gate; two unrelated selections come back nearly identical)
- **Location:** `chisurf/server/services/bursts.py:359-363` (span mode: `window[first : last + 1] = True`) and `:393` (`total_photons += int(per_bin.sum())`), surfaced as `n_photons` at `:415`
- **Finding:** in the default `span` mode the counted photons are *every* photon between the first and last gated one, which is intentional and documented — but the result reports that number as `n_photons` and carries **no field for the size of the gate**, so a caller reading the reply cannot tell that its selection contributed a small fraction of it. Verified on a 20 000-photon synthetic stream: a gate of **402** photons reports `n_photons = 19 101` and a completely disjoint gate of **22** photons reports `n_photons = 19 361`, with mean k of **19.938** and **19.939** — two different sub-populations, indistinguishable P(k). Because a burst explorer's "send selection to" menu exists to compare gated populations, the natural reading of two near-identical histograms is "these populations have the same brightness" when the truth is that neither result depends on the gate beyond its extent. Report the gated photon count (`index.size` after the channel/micro-time filter) alongside the counted one, and state in the result — as `interior` already does with `selection_bias` — that a span P(k) characterises the trace over the gate's extent rather than the gated photons.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-414
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S3 (the diagnostic that tells the caller how far the two PCH modes diverge can exceed 1, which its own docstring, guide and test say is impossible)
- **Location:** `chisurf/server/services/bursts.py:354-357` (the `for lo, hi in intervals` loop accumulating `burst_seconds`) against `:105-128` (`_selected_indices`, which deduplicates the same intervals) and `:419-422` (`burst_duty_cycle`)
- **Finding:** the photon selection is deduplicated but the duty-cycle accounting is not — `burst_seconds` sums the duration of every raw interval, so overlapping or repeated intervals are counted as many times as they appear while `span_seconds` is measured once. Verified: intervals `[[0, 4000], [2000, 6000]]` give **1.333**, and the same interval listed three times gives **3.0**, where the equivalent single interval `[[0, 6000]]` correctly gives 1.0. Overlapping intervals are not a hypothetical — `test_overlapping_intervals_are_not_double_counted` exists precisely because burst tables produce them — but `test_duty_cycle_reports_how_far_apart_the_two_modes_are` asserts `0.0 < duty <= 1.0` using only the two disjoint fixture intervals, and `docs/guides/52_send_bursts_to_analysis.md:108` states it is "the fraction of the span the bursts occupy". Measure the duration of the *union*: the covered photon indices are already computed as `index`, or merge the intervals before summing.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-415
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S3 (`interior` mode counts partially-observed burst-edge bins as if they were whole, inventing a low-k tail on top of the bias it does document)
- **Location:** `chisurf/server/services/bursts.py:377-390` (the `inside` mask: `b0 = int((macro[lo_c] - macro[first]) / bin_ticks)`, `b1 = ...`, `inside[max(0, b0) : min(n_bin, b1 + 1)] = True`)
- **Finding:** a bin that a burst only partly covers is marked `inside` and kept, but only the burst's photons are counted in it — so the bin reports a count for a shorter observation time than every other bin, exactly the "not observed" case the surrounding comment says the mask exists to exclude. There are two such bins per burst, and the module's whole argument for `interior` is that the *shape* of P(k) is comparable between gated populations. Verified on a stream with a perfectly constant 1 photon/µs rate and ten 1 ms bursts jittered off the 50 µs bin grid — the true P(k) is a delta at k = 50 — the service returns 192 bins at k = 50 plus **16 of 208 bins (8 %) smeared across k = 3…47**, pulling the mean from 50 to 48.08. With shorter bursts or wider bins the fraction grows linearly. Either drop the two edge bins per burst (keep only bins wholly inside an interval) or exclude them by comparing `b0`/`b1` against the exact interval boundaries; the current test only checks `n_photons`, which this bug preserves.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-416
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S3 (a channel number the file's routing dtype cannot represent crashes the read instead of selecting nothing)
- **Location:** `chisurf/server/services/bursts.py:131-135` (`_channel_filter`: `np.isin(channels, np.asarray(list(wanted), dtype=channels.dtype))`)
- **Finding:** the requested channel list is cast to the *file's* routing dtype, and `tttrlib` reports `routing_channels` as **int8** (verified on `test/data/clsm/PQ_Olympus_MFIS.ht3`: `dtype int8`, channels `[0 1 2 4 5]`). Under NumPy 2 an out-of-range Python int is an error, not a wrap, so asking for channel 130 raises `OverflowError: Python integer 130 out of bounds for int8`, which the blanket `except Exception` at `:224` turns into `OPERATION_FAILED` — `decay read failed: Python integer 130 out of bounds for int8`. A channel that is merely absent from the file behaves correctly (channel 3 returns the clean `INVALID_INPUT` "no photons in the gated intervals for the requested channels"), so the same class of request produces two different outcomes depending on a dtype the caller cannot see, and the message leaks NumPy internals over RPC. Compare in a wide integer type (`np.asarray(wanted, dtype=np.int64)` against `channels.astype(np.int64)`) so an unrepresentable channel simply matches nothing. `channels` arrives from an untrusted RPC caller. The same helper is used by both services.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-417
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S3 (the decay result's photon total counts a photon once per detector group that claims it)
- **Location:** `chisurf/server/services/bursts.py:222` (`used += int(mask.sum())` inside the per-group loop) surfaced as `n_photons` at `:253`
- **Finding:** `used` is accumulated per channel *group*, so a photon whose routing channel appears in two groups is added twice, and the top-level `n_photons` can exceed the number of photons the gate actually selected. Verified: a 1000-photon gate with `channels=[[0, 1], [0]]` reports `n_photons = 1518`. Overlapping groups are a normal request — a caller asking for "green", "red" and "all" in one call, or the polarised pair plus their sum — and the per-decay `n_photons` values are correct, so only the summary is wrong. Either count the union (`np.unique` over the matched indices) or document the field as the sum over groups; the current docstring (`:170-172`) says only `n_photons`, and no test asserts anything about it.
- **Fix note:**

## GUI tester — particle tracking (2026-07-27)

Drove *Microscopy → Imaging → Particle Tracking* headlessly against its own
ground-truth simulator, a real TIFF stack (`test/data/rics/RICS_EGFPGFP.tif`) and
a photon stream (`test/data/clsm/PQ_Olympus_MFIS.ht3`); see the use case
[particle tracking](/usecases/particle-tracking-diffusion.md). The science holds
up — 8 simulated particles at a true D of 0.5 px²/frame come back as
`0.5038 ± 0.1` in 1.7 s, with the honest "only 8 tracks contributed" caveat, and
a 50-frame 300×300 run stays responsive with a live status bar. What fails is
the reporting around it: the unit label follows a single "calibrated" boolean
covering two independent settings (RF-418), the report panel cannot wrap the
sentence that tells the user what to do next (RF-419), an empty *detection*
stage is diagnosed as a *linking* problem (RF-420), and a fit resting on 5 % of
21 954 shattered tracks prints no caveat at all (RF-421). Findings RF-418..RF-421.

### RF-418
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (a quotable physical number carries the wrong unit whenever only one of the two calibrations is entered)
- **Location:** `chisurf/plugins/microscopy/img_tracking/core.py:327` (`payload["calibrated"] = float(pixel_size) != 1.0 or float(frame_interval) != 1.0`), consumed at `:145` (`unit = "µm²/s" if self.info.get("calibrated") else "px²/frame"`) and `:155` (`length_unit = "µm" if ... else "px"`)
- **Finding:** one boolean covers **two independent** calibrations, and the report offers only the two extreme unit strings — there is no `px²/s` or `µm²/frame`. *Pixel size [µm]* and *Frame interval [s]* are separate fields with separate defaults of 1, so the mixed case is a normal thing to do: a user who works in pixels but knows the frame time enters only the interval. Verified through the GUI on the tool's own simulator (true D = 0.5 px²/frame): with **Pixel size left at its default 1.00000** and **Frame interval = 0.05 s** the report reads `D = 10.08 ± 2 µm²/s` and `localisation error = 0 µm`, where 10.077 = 0.5 / 0.05 is px²/s — the pixel size was never calibrated, so nothing in that number is in µm. The mirror case is just as wrong in principle: pixel 0.1 µm with the interval left at 1 reports `0.005038 µm²/s`, which is µm²/*frame* and only reads correctly because 1 frame happens to be spelt "1 s". `docs/guides/50_particle_tracking.md:99` documents only both-or-neither ("Set **Pixel size** and **Frame interval** and D comes out in µm²/s; leave them at 1 and it is in pixels² per frame"), so the mixed path is undocumented as well as mislabelled. Carry the two calibrations separately (`length_calibrated` / `time_calibrated`) and build the unit from them, `f"{'µm' if length else 'px'}²/{'s' if time else 'frame'}"`. While there: the status bar (`gui/tool.py:109-113`) and the `Net [px]` table column print D and displacements with **no** unit and a hard-coded `px` respectively, and are wrong in the same way. `TrackingResult.to_dict()` (`core.py:166`) hands the same ambiguous `calibrated` flag to the CLI and the RPC service.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-419
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S3 (the sentence telling the user what to do next is cut off at the panel edge in every window size tested)
- **Location:** `chisurf/plugins/microscopy/img_tracking/gui/view_model.py:204-208` (`results_html` returns `f"<pre style='margin:0'>{html.escape(self.results_text)}</pre>"`) rendered by `InfoWidget` (`chisurf/gui/autoform/sections/builtin.py:904-949`, `setHtml` with no wrap mode set)
- **Finding:** `<pre>` is pre-formatted text, so the report never wraps. The failure message built in `core.py:340-344` is **280 characters** on one line ("no track has at least 10 points; lower min_length or improve the linking before fitting transport. Longer tracks come from a larger max linking distance, a lower detection threshold, or gap closing — but check that they are still the same particle before trusting the D they give."). Verified by screenshot at 1500 × 950 **and** at 1920 × 1080: the Report panel shows a horizontal scrollbar and the text stops at "…Longer tracks come from a larger max linking distance, a" — the actionable half of the advice is off-screen, and a user reading the panel has no visual cue that anything follows. The same panel also clipped `alpha = 1 (fixed)` vertically mid-line once the persisted dock layout had shrunk it to ~90 px. `<pre>` is used only to keep the report's column alignment, which the report does not actually rely on: wrap it in `<div style='white-space:pre-wrap'>` (or set `setLineWrapMode(QTextEdit.WidgetWidth)` / `setWordWrapMode(QTextOption.WrapAtWordBoundaryOrAnywhere)` on the `InfoWidget`) and every line stays readable at any width. Worth checking the other `info` sections that feed `<pre>` through the same widget.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-420
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S3 (a run that detected nothing is diagnosed as a linking problem, sending the user to change the wrong three settings)
- **Location:** `chisurf/plugins/microscopy/img_tracking/core.py:333-344` (`analyse` catches `fit_msd`'s `ValueError` and appends the linking advice unconditionally), message text from `chisurf/core/fluorescence/imaging/tracking.py` `fit_msd` ("no track has at least {min_length} points; lower min_length or improve the linking before fitting transport")
- **Finding:** the only feedback a failed run gets is written for the case where tracks exist but are too short. When *detection* produced nothing, the same text still tells the user to lower `min_length`, raise the max linking distance or enable gap closing — none of which can help, because there is nothing to link. Verified through the GUI: `test/data/rics/RICS_EGFPGFP.tif` at the shipped default **Threshold 5 σ** reports `50 frames, 0 detections (0.0 per frame)` / `no tracks` and then the linking advice; the actual remedy is the threshold, and it is a cliff, not a slope — over 10 frames the same file gives 0 detections at 5 σ, 9 at 3 σ, 794 at 2 σ and 15 505 at 1 σ. The information needed to say the right thing is already in hand at `core.py:329` (`len(detections)` and `tracks.lengths()`), so branch on it: no detections → "no particle was detected — lower **Threshold [σ]**, or check **Min area** and the channel"; detections but no track ≥ `min_length` → the existing message. `test/` has no coverage of the zero-detection path.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-421
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S3 (a D fitted from noise is presented with no caveat, while a good fit from 8 clean tracks gets one)
- **Location:** `chisurf/core/fluorescence/imaging/tracking.py`, `MsdFit.warnings()` (checks `success`, `n_tracks < 20`, `relative_error > 0.25`, and an unresolved `alpha` — nothing else), surfaced by `TrackingResult.report()` at `chisurf/plugins/microscopy/img_tracking/core.py:159-163`
- **Finding:** the warning set has no check for how *badly linked* the tracks were, so the two numbers that say "this fit is junk" — the fraction of tracks that survived `min_track_length`, and the median track length — never reach the user. Verified through the GUI on `test/data/rics/RICS_EGFPGFP.tif` (RICS data of freely diffusing EGFP: nothing in it is trackable) with the threshold pushed to 1 σ: the report reads `50 frames, 77,796 detections (1555.9 per frame) / 21954 tracks, median length 3, longest 40 / D = 1.407 ± 0.35 px²/frame / from 1215 tracks over 9 MSD points` and prints **no "Read with care" block at all** — 94.5 % of the tracks were discarded, the median track is 3 points long, the detections are noise, and the only numeric guard (relative error) lands at 0.249, just under its 0.25 gate. By contrast the clean 8-track simulation *is* warned about, so the tool is most reassuring exactly when it is most wrong. The same blind spot shows on a simulation with a known answer: 200 particles at true D = 5 px²/frame (≈4.5 px/frame against a 5 px linking distance) returns `D = 2.812 ± 0.98` — 44 % low — with median track length 2 and 138 of 3187 tracks used, and only the generic 35 %-error note. Add two checks — the surviving fraction `fit.n_tracks / len(result.track_lengths())` below ~0.2, and a median track length within a point or two of `min_track_length`. `MsdFit.warnings()` does not know the total track count, so either hand it in (it already receives `min_length`) or raise the pair in `TrackingResult.report()`, which has both; phrase them as the guide already does — "the linking is shattering trajectories, which biases D low".
- **Fix note:**
## Review 2026-07-27 — AutoForm state: what a "restorable" form does not carry

Slice: `17d24d05e` (*every form is restorable from JSON, and burst folders use
it*) — `chisurf/gui/autoform/state.py`, the four new `AutoForm` methods and
`burst_manifest.restore_form`. The framing is right and the walk is correct:
`_CHILD_FIELDS = ("sections", "steps")` covers every container the spec has
(`PanelSection`, `DockAreaSection`, `WizardStepSection.sections`,
`WizardSection.steps` — there is no fifth), action-bound controls are rightly
skipped, and the commit's numbers check out exactly — 83 of 92 shipped specs,
690 bound controls, with **no** section carrying both `attr` and `set_action`
and none binding only through `call`.

What does not hold is the claim that this makes a form restorable. Three
classes of state a form really owns are dropped or restored wrongly, and none
of the 24 tests reaches any of them because the fixture spec is built from
plain `ValueSection`/`ChoiceSection`/`ToggleSection` only: toggle-row members
are not captured at all (RF-422), a control that declares a `call` is restored
by `setattr` alone, so the model method that derives everything from it never
runs (RF-423), and the `path_list` file list — a plain `list[str]` on the model
— is dropped from 10 otherwise-restorable specs (RF-424). Plus the manifest
side conflating `view_state` with `settings` (RF-425) and a capture path that
reports success after writing nothing (RF-426). Findings RF-422..RF-426.

### RF-422
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (the module documents toggle rows as captured; they are silently dropped in both directions)
- **Location:** `chisurf/gui/autoform/state.py:85-95` (`_key`: `attr = getattr(section, "attr", None)`) against `chisurf/core/dataspec/__init__.py:385-394` (`ToggleRowSection`, whose bindings live in `items`, not `attr`); the claim is at `state.py:14-16`
- **Finding:** the module docstring lists what is captured as "values, choices, toggles, **toggle rows**", but a `ToggleRowSection` carries no `attr` — each of its checkboxes is an `{"target", "attr", "label"}` entry in `items` — so `_key` returns `None`, `iter_bound_sections` never yields it, and the row is invisible to `collect_state` *and* `apply_state`. Verified with a two-section spec (one `ValueSection`, one `ToggleRowSection` over `corrections.correct_pile_up` / `corrections.reverse`): `collect_state` returns `{'n': 3}` with `correct_pile_up` set to `True`, and applying `{"corrections.correct_pile_up": True}` reports it under `unknown`, not `applied`. This is **14 controls in 6 shipped specs**, all of them settings a user would expect to survive: `core/models/tcspc/lifetime.view.json` and `mix_model.view.json` (`corrections.correct_pile_up`, `correct_dnl`, `reverse`), `core/models/pda2c/simple.view.json` (`pch0.absolute_amplitudes`, `normalize_amplitudes`), `core/experiments/ics/ics.view.json` (`fftshift`), `plugins/tttr/audifier` (`lt_log_tau`, `lt_log_amp`) and `plugins/tttr/tttr_splitter` (`split_files`, `reset_macro_times`, `keep_original`). Yield one pseudo-section (or one key) per `items` entry, `f"{item['target']}.{item['attr']}"` — the same key shape the individual `ToggleSection`s produce, so a row and a run of separate toggles round-trip identically.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-423
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (a restored value is written without the model method that makes it take effect, so the form shows the new setting while the model still holds the old derived numbers)
- **Location:** `chisurf/gui/autoform/state.py:226-228` (`apply_state`: `setattr(owner, section.attr, value)` and nothing else) against `chisurf/gui/autoform/sections/builtin.py:400-427` (`_BoundControlMixin._commit`, which does the `setattr` **and then** `getattr(self._model, call)(value)` followed by `_refresh_host_form()`)
- **Finding:** every interactive edit of a `call`-bearing control runs the model method; a restore never does. Verified with a stub bound as `ChoiceSection(attr="donor_dye", call="apply_dye_selection")`: after `apply_state({"donor_dye": "A594"})` the attribute is `"A594"`, the derived value is untouched and the call count is **0**. **50 bound controls in 11 shipped specs** declare a `call`, and in several the call *is* the semantics: `plugins/burst/accurate_fret` binds `donor_dye`, `acceptor_dye`, `kappa2` and `refractive_index` to `apply_dye_selection`, which is what pulls R0, the quantum yields and τ_D(0) out of the dye database (`gui/view_model.py:295-320`) — a restored form therefore shows the restored dye pair beside the *previous* pair's R0, which is a wrong number rather than a stale label; `plugins/microscopy/clsm` binds `filename` to `load_file` (`gui/view_model.py:153-171`), so the tool names a file it never opened; `plugins/ai_settings` binds `api_key`→`apply_token` and `provider`→`set_provider`; `gui/widgets/synthetic_decay_editor.view.json` and `fret_species_editor.view.json` route 13 fields through `field_changed`. `sync_fields()` only pushes model → widget, so the divergence is invisible in the GUI. Invoke `call` after the `setattr` (collecting the distinct calls and firing each once at the end avoids re-running an expensive loader per field), and report a raising call in `StateResult.failed` rather than silently.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-424
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (ten otherwise-restorable tools save and restore every setting and come back with no input files)
- **Location:** `chisurf/gui/autoform/state.py:85-89` (`_key` requires `attr`, and a `custom` section has none) against `chisurf/gui/autoform/sections/path_list_section.py:190-202` (`_current` reads `getattr(self._model, self._target)`, `_commit` writes `setattr(self._model, self._target, committed)`), and the justification at `state.py:17-19`
- **Finding:** the reason given for skipping `custom` sections — their "widgets own their own values" — is false for `path_list`, the unified file/folder list: its value is a plain `list[str]` **on the model**, addressed by `target` (see [[viewjson-custom-sections-bind-by-target]]), and is exactly as JSON-safe as any `ValueSection`. Because `_key` keys off `attr`, it is dropped. **12 shipped specs** declare a `path_list`, **10 of them alongside other bound controls**, so they are counted among the 83 "restorable" specs while losing the one thing that says what the analysis ran on: `burst_gs` (`bur_files`, 25 other controls), `sm_image_mle` (`sel_files`, `sel_irf_files`, 22), `img_pixel_mle` (same two, 17), `tttr_lut_tools` (`files`, 11), `clsm_generator` (`sel_lifetime_files`, 10), `img_calibration` (`sel_irf_files`, 9), `burst_irf_bg` / `ptu_alex_creator` / `tttr_splitter` (5 each) and `batch_analysis` (2). For a batch tool the file list *is* the analysis. Let a `custom` section opt into state by declaring its key in a small allow-list (`path_list`, and `region_list` once `RegionCollection` has a JSON form) with the state key taken from `target`, or add an explicit `stateful: true` flag to `CustomSection` — either way the collector must stop claiming coverage it does not have.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-425
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S3 (the manifest's own docstring says the two mappings must not be conflated; `restore_form` conflates them)
- **Location:** `chisurf/core/fio/fluorescence/burst_manifest.py:317` (`stored = manifest.get("view_state") or manifest.get("settings")`) against `:147-151` (the `view_state` parameter doc: stored separately "because it restores *the form*, key for key, where ``settings`` records what the analysis actually used … and must not be conflated when they do not [agree]")
- **Finding:** when a folder has no `view_state` — every folder written by the shipped writer, `burst_selection.api.selection.analyze_file` (`:524-539`), which passes `settings=` only — `restore_form` hands the **analysis settings** to `apply_state` as though they were form state. The two key spaces are unrelated: `_manifest_settings` (`selection.py:45-53`) is `asdict(AnalysisSettings)`, i.e. top-level names like `output_formats`, `photon_filter`, `burst_filter`, `gmm` whose values are nested dicts, while an AutoForm key is `<target>.<attr>`. In the ordinary case every key lands in `unknown` and the restore is a no-op that still returns a `StateResult` (so a caller showing `summary()` says "0 setting(s) restored"), but a form binding a top-level attribute of the same name gets the nested settings dict written straight onto it by `setattr` and reported as `applied`. Return `None` when there is no `view_state`, or apply the fallback only for keys the form actually knows (`known` is already built inside `apply_state`).
- **Fix note:**

### RF-426
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S3 (the capture direction cannot fail: it writes an empty settings file and returns its path as though it had worked)
- **Location:** `chisurf/gui/autoform/state.py:288-313` (`_spec_of`, whose `except Exception: continue` swallows a `view_spec` that cannot be called), `:164-167` (`collect_state` returns `{}` when the spec is `None`) and `:240-262` (`save_state` writes that and returns the path)
- **Finding:** the apply direction reports an unresolvable spec (everything lands in `unknown`, `result.ok` is `False`); the capture direction reports nothing at all. Verified with a model whose `view_spec` takes a required argument — the case `_spec_of`'s own comment anticipates ("a model may need arguments") — `save_state` writes `{"format": "chisurf-autoform-state", "state": {}, "version": 1}` and returns the path, with no log line at any level. The same silence covers a caller that passes something that is not a form at all (`form: Any`; `restore_form(object(), …)` is already exercised in `test/core/test_burst_manifest.py`). A settings file that stores nothing is discovered only later, when restoring it changes nothing. Distinguish "no bound controls" from "no spec" — log a warning in `collect_state` when `_spec_of` returns `None`, and record the reason `_spec_of` discarded each candidate rather than dropping the exception.
- **Fix note:**

## Review 2026-07-27 (2) — chimol voxel maps: a first-class object the GUI never makes

Slice: `b773f96ff` (*voxel maps as first-class objects, and an MRC reader that
places them correctly*) — `chimol/volume.py`, `chimol/io/mrc.py`,
`chimol/cmd/volumes.py` and the `MolView` half of `renderer/view.py`, against
`chimol/test/test_volume.py` (37 tests) and the new guide-44 section.

The MRC reader itself holds up: the `mapc/mapr/maps` permutation is applied the
right way round (`samples` is `[s, r, c]`, so spatial axis `a` really does sit on
array axis `2 - ijk_to_crs[a]`), the origin preference matches the reference
reader, `step` needs no permutation because `mx`/`xlen` are already in xyz, and
`strided()` scales the step with the stride so a subsampled map stays in place.
`index_to_world` and `isosurface` apply the same `R·(idx·step) + origin`, so
there is one placement rule rather than two.

What does not hold is everything around the object. The frame-sharing fix works
in one order only — load the map *first* and it is drawn on top of the model
again (RF-427) — and the GUI's own *File → Open* never makes a map object at all,
so none of `isosurface`/`isomesh`/`volume_level`/`map_info` can see a map a user
opened (RF-428). The level check and the drawing disagree about which grid they
are checking against, so a big map answers "at 50" and draws nothing (RF-429);
the contour is re-run by marching cubes on every redraw, 0.34–0.6 s per unrelated
click (RF-430); and the `name` every contour is given is stored and read nowhere
(RF-431). Findings RF-427..RF-431.

### RF-427
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S1 (a density is drawn centred on the model instead of where the file puts it, whenever the map is loaded before the structure)
- **Location:** `chisurf/plugins/chimol/chimol/renderer/view.py:6845-6856` (`add_volume`, the `shared_centre` loop and `state.raw_center = centre_world if shared_centre is None else shared_centre`) against `:2160-2162` and `:2318-2319` (`set_structure` / `set_coordinates`, each of which sets its own object's `_raw_center` from its own centroid and reframes nothing)
- **Finding:** the fix the commit describes ("a map now adopts the frame of whatever is already loaded") only runs inside `add_volume`, so it covers `load model.pdb` → `load_map density.mrc` and not the reverse. Nothing reframes a map when a structure is loaded *after* it: `add_structure`/`add_coordinates` set the new object's `raw_center` to its own centroid, and the only reframing seam, `_reframe_to` (`:1538`), is called from `create_from_selection` and `_remove_atoms` only. Verified headlessly with a 24³ map (centre 11.5, 11.5, 11.5) and a 4-atom structure sitting in one corner of it (centre 4, 4, 4), scale 10: loading the structure first puts the contour's centroid at scene `(80, 80, 80)` and the atoms at `(0, 3.03, 1.51)` — 8 Å apart, correct — while loading the **map first** puts the contour's centroid at `(5, 5, 5)`, i.e. on top of the atoms, which is exactly the "density that wraps a structure appears as a small blob inside it" failure the commit says it fixed. `load_map density.mrc` then `load model.pdb` is an ordinary session opening, and the guide's own example order (`load_map` first, `isomesh` second) invites it. Either reframe every existing map to the new structure's centre when one is loaded (`_reframe_to` already exists, but only shifts `_coords`/`_all_atom_coords`, so a map needs its `raw_center` moved and the contour rebuilt), or give the scene one frame instead of a per-object one. `test_a_map_adopts_the_frame_of_what_is_already_loaded` (`test/test_volume.py:439`) pins only the working order.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-428
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (a map opened the only way the GUI offers is not a map object, so every command the commit adds reports that no maps are loaded)
- **Location:** `chisurf/plugins/chimol/chimol/app/molview_main_window.py:1636-1677` (the `is_map` branch: `points, meta = load_mrc_as_points(path)` → `self.viewer.add_coordinates(...)` → `set_dots_visible(True)`), reachable from the open dialog's filter at `:658` (`*.mrc *.map *.ccp4 *.mrc.gz *.map.gz *.ccp4.gz`)
- **Finding:** `add_volume` has exactly one caller in the tree, `cmd/volumes.py:69` (`load_map`); `grep -rn 'load_map\|add_volume' chimol/app/` returns nothing. *File → Open* on an MRC therefore still takes the legacy point-cloud path and creates an ordinary **coordinates** object of up to 250 000 fake atoms rendered as dots — `entry.state.volume` stays `None`, so `_resolve_map_object` (`cmd/volumes.py:242-250`) finds no maps and `isosurface`, `isomesh`, `volume_level` and `map_info` all answer "*no maps are loaded; `load_map file.mrc` reads one*" for a map that is plainly on screen. Two further consequences follow from it being a coordinates object: it carries its own `raw_center` and so is misplaced exactly as in [RF-427], and it is thinned to a point cloud at one hard-coded contour with no way to move the level. Guide 44's new section documents only the command-line form, so the GUI opener and the documented behaviour have silently forked. Route the `is_map` branch through `load_mrc_grid` + `viewer.add_volume`, and keep `load_mrc_as_points` for callers that genuinely want points.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-429
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (the command validates the level against the full map and the renderer against the strided one, so a level the command accepts and reports can draw nothing at all)
- **Location:** `chisurf/plugins/chimol/chimol/cmd/volumes.py:105-126` (`_contour`: `low, high = grid.value_range()` on the full grid, then the success message) and `:179-184` (`volume_level`, the same check) against `chisurf/plugins/chimol/chimol/volume.py:298-304` (`isosurface`: `grid = self.strided(voxel_limit_m)` **then** `low, high = grid.value_range()`)
- **Finding:** striding drops the peaks, so the strided grid's range is a subset of the full one and the two checks disagree for every map over the 16 M-voxel budget. Verified headlessly on a 260³ map (17.6 M voxels, stride 2) holding a sharp peak on odd indices: full range `0 … 100`, strided range `0 … 9.60`. `isosurface mymesh, sharp, 50` passes the command's `low < 50 < high`, prints `isosurface: sharp at 50 (0.0% of voxels)` on the **message** callback with the error callback empty, stores the level, and then `_update_volume` gets `None` back from `grid.isosurface(50.0)` and `continue`s — `view._scene.objects` is `[]`. That is precisely the "quietly drawing nothing" the commit and the guide say cannot happen ("*a level outside it is refused **with** the range rather than quietly drawing nothing*", `docs/guides/44_molecular_viewer.md`). The reported voxel fraction is computed on the full grid too, so it describes a surface that was never drawn. Check the level against the grid that will actually be contoured — `grid.strided(voxel_limit_m).value_range()` — and say so in the refusal ("*at the stride this map is drawn at, values only reach 9.6*"), since the honest answer is about the display budget, not the data.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-430
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (every unrelated redraw re-runs marching cubes over the whole map; 0.34–0.6 s per click with one 8 M-voxel map loaded)
- **Location:** `chisurf/plugins/chimol/chimol/renderer/view.py:6889-6970` (`_update_volume`, which calls `grid.isosurface(level)` unconditionally) called from `:6678` (`_build_scene_for_current_object`) inside the per-object loop of `_update_view` (`:6612-6673`)
- **Finding:** nothing memoises the contour: the mesh is rebuilt from the voxels on every `_update_view`, although neither the grid nor the level changed. Measured headlessly on a 200³ Gaussian map (8.0 M voxels, stride 1, 48 030 contour vertices) with numba warm: three successive bare `_update_view()` calls took 0.534 s, 0.511 s and 0.603 s. With a small structure alongside it, ordinary interactions that touch no map at all cost the same — `set_active_object` 0.345 s, `set_selected_residues` 0.342 s, `set_object_visible` 0.418 s. `MolView` has **54** `self._update_view(` call sites, including `handle_mouse_click` (`:3484`), `set_frame_position` (`:1181`) and `set_active_frame` (`:2475`), so every pick and every trajectory frame pays it; a map at the 16 M ceiling costs roughly twice as much. The guide claims the voxel budget is what keeps "*a contour change quick*" — the budget bounds one contour, not the number of times it is recomputed. Cache `(verts, faces, normals)` per `(id(grid), level, voxel_limit_m, style)` on the object state and invalidate it in `add_volume`/`set_volume_levels`, which are the only two places either input changes.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-431
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S3 (the first positional argument of `isosurface`/`isomesh` is stored and read nowhere, so a contour cannot be addressed by the name PyMOL's contract gives it)
- **Location:** `chisurf/plugins/chimol/chimol/cmd/volumes.py:113-121` (`_contour` writes `"name": name or f"{style}_{len(levels) + 1}"` into the level dict) against `chisurf/plugins/chimol/chimol/renderer/view.py:6903-6968` (`_update_volume`, which reads `level`, `color` and `style` only and ids its scene objects `f"volume_{index}"`) and `cmd/volumes.py:189-191` (`volume_level`, which rewrites the level list without the key)
- **Finding:** `grep -rn` for the key shows it written in one place and read in none. In PyMOL `isomesh dens, map, 0.08` creates an *object* called `dens` that `color`, `disable`, `enable` and `delete` then address; here the name is a label on a dict that never leaves the state, the scene object is called `volume_0`/`volume_1` by position, and `volume_level` drops it on the first replacement — so there is no way to recolour or remove one contour of a multi-level map, which is the case the feature exists for ("*a dense core inside a diffuse shell*", `renderer/chimol_state.py:82-84`). The module docstring opens by claiming "PyMOL's names and argument order, per the compatibility contract", which makes the silence worse than a missing argument would be. Either use the name — id the scene object `f"{object_prefix}:{name}"` and let the existing object commands resolve it — or drop the parameter and say in the guide that contours are addressed by level.
- **Fix note:**


## Crash report — the burst pipeline died on 2CDE (2026-07-27)

A user-supplied macOS crash report (SIGBUS, ``EXC_ARM_DA_ALIGN`` at 0x109, main
thread) taken while stepping to *4. 2CDE* in the burst-analysis shell. The stack
is five repetitions of ``QCoreApplication::notifyInternal2`` →
``QObject::event`` → ``PyQtSlotProxy::qt_metacall`` → Python →
``cfunction_call`` → ``notifyInternal2``, dying inside
``QCoreApplication::postEvent``. RF-432, RF-433.

### RF-432
- **Status:** FIXED
- **Severity:** S1 (the burst pipeline crashes the whole application, losing the session)
- **Location:** `chisurf/gui/widgets/navigation.py` (`_on_log_status` and the six other bare `QCoreApplication.processEvents()` calls in the status-bar API), `chisurf/gui/progress.py` (`ChiSurfProgress._process_events`), `chisurf/plugins/burst/burst_bva/gui/tool.py:_status`, `chisurf/plugins/burst/burst_h2mm/gui/tool.py:_status`
- **Finding:** Every status write pumped the event loop unguarded. `processEvents` *dispatches queued work*, and one of the things queued is the shell's own `status_logged` signal — emitted by `_StatusLogHandler` from whichever thread logged. So a status update delivers a log record, whose slot writes the status bar, which pumps again: each round adds a `PyQtSlotProxy::qt_metacall` → Python → `notifyInternal2` frame to the C stack, which is exactly the repeating pattern in the report. Reproduced headlessly: with the guard removed, one `logger.info` from a shell with a status logger nests **6** pumps deep before the harness stops it. Two consequences ride on the same defect — the pump also delivers *clicks*, so a user switching panel or closing the window mid-analysis destroys the widgets the running operation still writes to, which is the shape of a dangling receiver in `postEvent`.
- **Fix note:** One shared, process-wide guarded pump — the new
  `chisurf/gui/event_pump.py` (`pump_ui(allow_input=…)`) — replaces every bare
  `processEvents` in the status/progress path. The guard has to be process-wide
  because the hazard is the shared C stack, and the pumps sit in four different
  objects. Callers that need a clickable Cancel keep input; the log-driven
  caption update and the tools' own `_status` helpers pass
  `allow_input=False`, so a click can no longer be delivered into a running
  analysis. Verified by driving the burst shell headlessly to the 2CDE step on a
  real 2495-burst folder: the step runs (2343 valid) and the pump depth stays
  1. Pinned by `test/gui/test_event_pump.py` (nesting, guard release on error,
  input policy) and two cases in `test/gui/test_navigation_statusbar.py`; the
  nesting test reproduces "nested 6 deep" against the pre-fix behaviour.

### RF-433
- **Status:** FIXED
- **Severity:** S2 (the selected workflow step has no visible label — the shell shows which step you are on only by its emoji)
- **Location:** `chisurf/gui/widgets/navigation.py:440-456` (the `nav_list` style sheet: a `QListWidget::item` rule with no `:selected` counterpart)
- **Finding:** Found by inspecting the render of the burst shell while verifying RF-432: the current step, *4. 2CDE*, showed its icon and no text. Styling `::item` at all hands item painting to the style-sheet style, which then draws no selection background, and the label is painted in the palette's `HighlightedText` — white — on the plain white viewport. Measured on a freshly built shell: the selected row is 5987 white pixels with no highlight colour anywhere in it. Every `NavigationPanelTool` shell is affected (burst analysis, FCS, TTTR, imaging).
- **Fix note:** Added explicit `::item:selected` (palette highlight + highlighted
  text) and `::item:hover:!selected` rules, so both themes stay legible. The same
  measurement now reports 4172 highlight pixels and 1506 text pixels. Pinned by
  `test_selected_step_stays_readable` in `test/gui/test_navigation_search.py`,
  which grabs the list and asserts both colours are present in the selected row.

## QA run 2026-07-27 (2) — DEER distance distribution, driven through the GUI

Workflow: [DEER/PELDOR distance distribution](/usecases/deer-distance-distribution.md).
Five headless passes over the real main window with the three `test/data/deer/`
fixtures and all four DEER models. The science holds — a clean CSV trace fits to
χ²ᵣ = 1.206 with random residuals, and Tikhonov resolves the second population of
`deer_twostate` where a single Gaussian cannot. What surrounds it does not: two
of the four models show their shape parameters as raw HTML entities, every
parameter table slices its last row, the reader's three switches have no control
at all, every new fit opens on an unevaluated model reporting χ²ᵣ = 30113, and
the MaxEnt inversion under-fits the trace worse than a two-parameter Gaussian.
Findings RF-432..RF-436.

### RF-432
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (parameter labels that are pure HTML entities are printed as their source text, in every model editor in the app)
- **Location:** `chisurf/gui/widgets/chitable/delegates.py:34-36` (`RichTextDelegate.paint`: `if not text or "<" not in str(text): return super().paint(...)`), reached from `chisurf/gui/autoform/sections/parameter_table.py:434-435` (the `COL_NAME` delegate) with the display text from `:199` (`_display_value` returns `label_text` verbatim)
- **Finding:** the delegate decides whether a cell needs HTML by testing for `<`, so a label made only of character entities never reaches `QTextDocument.setHtml` and is drawn as plain text. Verified headlessly on a `DeerRiceModel` editor: the two shape parameters of the model render as **`&nu;[&#8491;]`** and **`&sigma;[&#8491;]`**, the modulation depth as `&lambda;` and the regularisation weight as `&alpha;`, while `t<sub>0</sub>[µs]` and `k[µs<sup>-1</sup>]` in the same tables render correctly (they contain `<`) — screenshot `4R_editor.png`, and `m.data(m.index(i,0))` returns exactly those strings. The Rice model has only two distance parameters and *both* are unreadable. Not DEER-specific: `grep -rn 'label_text="&' chisurf/core/models/` finds entity-only labels in `deer/deer.py` (`&lambda;`, `&alpha;`, `&nu;[&#8491;]`, `&sigma;[&#8491;]`), `fcs/general.py` and `fcs/mdf.py` (`&epsilon;[kHz]`) and `pda2c/saw_nu.py` (`&nu;`). Fix in the delegate, not the labels: test for `<` **or** `&`, or simply always route through the text document (the fast path exists for cost, and a cheap `("<" in t or "&" in t)` keeps it).
- **Fix note:**

### RF-433
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (every parameter-group table in every AutoForm model editor clips its last row; a two-row group shows the second parameter as a half-height smear)
- **Location:** `chisurf/gui/autoform/sections/parameter_table.py:492-496` (`_size_to_content`: `setFixedHeight(header_h + self._row_h * max(1, n) + 2)`) and the identical copy at `:1109-1113` for the paired table; `self._row_h = table_row_height()` at `:385` / `:973`
- **Finding:** the height is budgeted with the *nominal* row height while the rows are laid out at their real height, so the fixed height is short by `(actual - nominal) × n`. Measured headlessly on a `DeerRiceModel` editor (`build_model_editor`, 471 × 620): `_row_h = 18` and `_header_h = 18`, but `rowHeight(i) = 24` for every row and `horizontalHeader().height() = 21`. The 2-row *Distance (Rice)* table gets `setFixedHeight(21 + 36 + 2) = 59` where the content needs `21 + 48 + 2 = 71` — **12 px short**, and the 3-row *Modulation* and *Distance grid* tables get 77 against 95, **18 px short**. The clipping is plainly visible (`4R_editor.png`: `&sigma;` is cut at ~40 % height under `&nu;`) and there is no scrollbar and 275 px of unused dock underneath, so the space is available. Size from the view's own metrics — `horizontalHeader().height() + sum(rowHeight(i)) + 2 * frameWidth()` — or call `resizeRowsToContents()` first and read back.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-434
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (three reader settings that exist in the API have no control in the GUI; the controller silently swallows the failure)
- **Location:** `chisurf/core/experiments/deer/reader.py:70-100` (`DeerReader.__init__` — `phase_correction`, `normalize`, `exp_type`) against `chisurf/gui/widgets/experiments/deer/__init__.py:36-42` (`if reader_obj is not None and hasattr(reader_obj, "view_spec"): … except Exception: pass`); no `chisurf/core/experiments/deer/*.view.json` exists
- **Finding:** the controller's own docstring says it "renders the reader's AutoForm settings (phase correction, normalisation, experiment type) when available", but `chisurf/core/experiments/deer/` has no view spec — every other experiment reader ships one (`tcspc_csv.view.json`, `tcspc_tttr.view.json`, `fcs.view.json`, `pch.view.json`, `pda.view.json`, `ics.view.json`) — so `hasattr(reader_obj, "view_spec")` is False and the AutoForm is never built. Verified headlessly: with `Experiment = DEER` selected, `ctrl.findChildren(...)` for `QCheckBox | QComboBox | QLineEdit | QSpinBox | QDoubleSpinBox` returns **`[]`** and the controller's whole child list is `['QVBoxLayout', 'QLabel']`; the *File parameters* section shows one hint line above ~700 px of empty dock (`01_read_data_dock.png`). Consequence: a user cannot disable the automatic zero-order phasing on a trace it gets wrong, cannot keep an un-normalised trace un-normalised, and cannot record the experiment type — all three are constructor arguments that only a script can reach. Add `deer.view.json` with the three controls (each with a `description`) and let the existing branch render it; the bare `except: pass` should also log, since it is what hid this.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-435
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (every new DEER fit opens reporting χ²ᵣ = 30113.93 against a model curve of zeros, indistinguishable from a catastrophic mismatch)
- **Location:** `chisurf/core/models/deer/deer.py:411-423` (`_DeerModelBase.update_model`, never called between fit creation and the first **Fit**) — the fit sub-window therefore renders `ModelCurve`'s zero-filled `y`
- **Finding:** verified on the stock app (no RPC port override) for all four DEER models: immediately after **Add fit**, `np.asarray(fit.model.y)` is `min = max = 0` over all 588 points and the *Fit* tab annotation reads `chi2r=30113.9309, DW=0.0001` with the model drawn as a flat line at zero and weighted residuals of 150 … 340 (`30_new_fit_window.png`, `05_main_after_addfit.png`). The model is *not* mis-parameterised — `_DeerModelBase.__init__` seeds t₀ from the reader metadata and λ from the tail plateau, and a manual `model.update()` immediately gives `y ∈ [0.359, 1]` and χ²ᵣ = 560.9 — it has simply never been evaluated. The same window shows a fully computed **L-Curve** tab for the model-free models, so the α-scan runs at creation while the model curve does not, which makes the zero line read as a result rather than a placeholder. Evaluate the model once when the fit is created (or when its sub-window is first shown) so the opening χ²ᵣ is the start-value χ²ᵣ.
- **Fix note:**

### RF-436
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Severity:** S2 (the maximum-entropy inversion under-fits the data worse than a two-parameter model and returns an over-smoothed P(r))
- **Location:** `chisurf/core/models/deer/maxent.py:143-175` (the α auto-selection: `alphas = np.logspace(-3, 1.3, n_alpha)` and the discrepancy rule "pick the LARGEST alpha whose misfit is acceptable") reached from `chisurf/core/models/deer/deer.py:612-621` (`DeerMaxEntModel._distribution`)
- **Finding:** driven through the GUI on `test/data/deer/deer_twostate.DSC` (588 points, reader noise estimate σ = 3.00e-3, which `_noise_level()` does read — t₀ seeding from the same metadata works), with default settings and α = 0 (auto), the MaxEnt model stops at **χ²ᵣ = 20.5230** after 62 s, while the Tikhonov model on the identical trace reaches **6.8387** and a *single Gaussian* reaches **8.9672**. A model-free inversion being beaten by a two-parameter shape is the signature of too much smoothing, and the returned distribution confirms it: `P(r)` is one broad peak at ≈ 37.5 Å sitting on a **uniform 0.007 pedestal across the entire 15 … 65 Å grid** (`4M_distribution.png`) — the flat entropy prior, undamped — where Tikhonov resolves the peak at 36.5 Å plus a shoulder at ≈ 46 Å and a minor peak at ≈ 24 Å (`23_tab1_Distribution.png`). Either the discrepancy target is being computed against the wrong scale or the "largest acceptable α" rule needs the misfit criterion the Tikhonov side gets from GCV/L-curve; whichever it is, a user offered two model-free models has no way to tell that one of them is not converging.
- **Fix note:**

  delegate must be under half the width the base `QStyledItemDelegate` paints for the
  same string (one glyph, not four). Against the pre-fix delegate the test reports
  `35px == 35px` and fails.

### RF-433
- **Status:** OPEN

- **Location:** `chisurf/gui/autoform/sections/parameter_table.py:492-496` (`_size_to_content`: `setFixedHeight(header_h + self._row_h * max(1, n) + 2)`) and the identical copy at `:1109-1113` for the paired table; `self._row_h = table_row_height()` at `:385` / `:973`

Measured headlessly on a `DeerRiceModel` editor (`build_model_editor`, 471 × 620): `_row_h = 18` and `_header_h = 18`, but `rowHeight(i) = 24` for every row and `horizontalHeader().height() = 21`. The 2-row *Distance (Rice)* table gets `setFixedHeight(21 + 36 + 2) = 59` where the content needs `21 + 48 + 2 = 71` — **12 px short**, and the 3-row *Modulation* and *Distance grid* tables get 77 against 95, **18 px short**. The clipping is plainly visible (`4R_editor.png`: `&sigma;` is cut at ~40 % height under `&nu;`) and there is no scrollbar and 275 px of unused dock underneath, so the space is available. Size from the view's own metrics — `horizontalHeader().height() + sum(rowHeight(i)) + 2 * frameWidth()` — or call `resizeRowsToContents()` first and read back.

### RF-434

Consequence: a user cannot disable the automatic zero-order phasing on a trace it gets wrong, cannot keep an un-normalised trace un-normalised, and cannot record the experiment type — all three are constructor arguments that only a script can reach. Add `deer.view.json` with the three controls (each with a `description`) and let the existing branch render it; the bare `except: pass` should also log, since it is what hid this.
